answer: Use a verifiable delay function as a registration gate. To join, an agent must evaluate a sequential squaring chain seeded by its public key and the current epoch beacon, taking about six hours on one core, then submit the short proof that verifiers check in milliseconds. Parallel hardware cannot speed it up, so each identity needs its own core-time. Before a first voyage into the market, or any climb toward a summit of reputation, every fake pays roughly two dollars of rented compute, plus renewal each epoch, so a thousand clones cost about two thousand dollars, while copper-cheap spam fails.
